cards.vorderseite: Spinal AVM/AVF: most common type, presentation, treatment
cards.rueckseite: **Dural AVF** most common: dural artery → spinal (radicular) vein in the intervertebral foramen. 80% progressive myelopathy/back pain, 20% acute (hemorrhage). **Foix–Alajouanine syndrome** (venous congestive myelopathy). MRA/CTA to localize, then catheter angiography. Treatment: **disconnection of the draining vein** (surgery), sometimes embolization.

cards.vorderseite: Spinal epidural hematoma: causes and management
cards.rueckseite: Traumatic (incl. after LP with coagulopathy) or spontaneous (~⅓ anticoagulation); low cervical/thoracolumbar. Acute back pain → rapidly progressive myelopathy. **Reverse coagulopathy**; urgent decompressive laminectomy unless pain only. Better recovery with decompression early (esp. **< 48 h**).

cards.vorderseite: Spinal epidural abscess: key facts and treatment
cards.rueckseite:
Location: 50% thoracic, 30% lumbar, 20% cervical. Risk factors: **diabetes, IV drug use**, renal failure, alcohol. Triad: **back pain, fever, local tenderness**; myelopathy can develop rapidly.
**Early surgery + antibiotics** (~6 wk IV, then ~6 wk oral) if weakness, incontinence, instability or plegia < 72 h. Antibiotics alone only if neurologically intact (or plegia > 72 h) and stable; operate on deterioration.

cards.vorderseite: Diskitis: organisms, diagnosis, treatment
cards.rueckseite: **S. aureus** > S. epidermidis (most common postop) > gram-negatives (**Pseudomonas in IV drug users**). Postop < 0.5%, weeks after surgery. Pain/tenderness; fever in < 50%. **ESR/CRP** highly sensitive. CT-guided aspiration ~60% positive. ~75% cured with antibiotics (6 wk IV + 6 wk oral) and immobilization; surgery for diagnosis, decompression or instability.

cards.vorderseite: Vertebral osteomyelitis: key facts
cards.rueckseite: Lumbar > thoracic > cervical. **S. aureus** ≫ E. coli. Most common source: **genitourinary tract**. TB = **Pott's disease**. Blood cultures positive ~50%, needle aspirate ~60%. ~90% treated with antibiotics + immobilization.

zeilen: 45% (most common in adults); NF2; cervical, filum (myxopapillary)
Distinct plane → complete resection, low recurrence
Indistinct plane; ~25% malignant in adults; LGA 5-y survival 50%
Dorsal location → early proprioceptive loss; complete resection

cards.vorderseite: Intramedullary tumor surgery: most important predictor of postoperative function
cards.rueckseite: The **preoperative neurologic status**. Resection with intraoperative neuromonitoring; adjuvant radiation reserved for high-grade or multiply recurrent tumors.

zeilen: No sex predilection, peak 30 y, NF2
Total excision rarely possible without deficit; malignant change 5–10% in NF1

cards.vorderseite: Myeloma / plasmacytoma of the spine: workup and treatment
cards.rueckseite:
Workup: skeletal survey, serum/urine **protein electrophoresis** (Bence–Jones), calcium (hypercalcemia), CBC, coagulation. ~50% of plasmacytomas progress to myeloma within 5 y.
Treatment: **radiotherapy first** (control > 90%) unless rapid neurologic deterioration or instability → resection/fusion; chemotherapy for myeloma.

cards.text: Spinal metastases: {{c1::95%}} extradural; most common primaries {{c2::breast and lung (20% each)}}, then {{c3::prostate (10%)}}. First symptom is {{c4::pain (90%)}}.

cards.vorderseite: Metastatic spinal cord compression: surgery vs. radiation
cards.rueckseite:
**Steroids** (dexamethasone 10 mg, then 16 mg/day).
**Radiation alone:** radiosensitive tumors (**lymphoma, myeloma**), life expectancy < 3–4 months, diffuse disease, high surgical risk, complete deficit > 48 h.
**Surgery + radiation:** single-level compression, radiotherapy failure, instability/bony compression, unknown diagnosis. Patchell trial: ambulatory 84% vs 57%, regained ambulation 62% vs 19%.
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 629, Table 6.20. Today also SINS score and NOMS framework, SBRT.

cards.vorderseite: Cervical disk disease: levels and treatment
cards.rueckseite: **C6–C7 (70%)**, C5–C6 (25%). Soft disk in the young (mostly improves spontaneously), osteophytes in the elderly (often progressive). Conservative first: **95% recover** from acute radiculopathy. Surgery: ACDF, posterior keyhole foraminotomy (far lateral disk), laminectomy (multilevel). Postop **C5 palsy** up to 3%; adjacent segment degeneration.

cards.vorderseite: Thoracic disk herniation: features and surgical approach
cards.rueckseite: 75% at **T8–T12**. Back/radicular pain 60%, sensory 25%, myelopathy 20%. **Never retract the cord**: laminectomy has the worst results. Posterolateral (transpedicular, costotransversectomy) or **anterior/transthoracic** (best results): upper thoracic from the **right** (heart), lower thoracic from the **left** (aorta easier to mobilize, liver in the way).

cards.vorderseite: Lumbar disk herniation: natural history and surgery
cards.rueckseite: 75% improve by 1 month, > 85% overall → conservative first, unless **cauda equina syndrome** (emergency) or progressive deficit. Surgery if no improvement after **6–12 weeks** (90–95% effective). Complications: infection 0.5–2%, motor deficit 1–8%, dural tear 1–5%, reherniation 5%. Surgery better at 1 year, **little difference at 4 years**.

cards.vorderseite: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy: outcome and approach
cards.rueckseite: Most common myelopathy > 55 y; **ALS** can mimic. Improvement with surgery ~50% if symptoms < 1 year, 16% if > 1 year. Bracing only temporizes. **Anterior** (ACDF) for anterior compression at 1–2 levels; **posterior** laminectomy ± fusion (or laminoplasty) for ≥ 3 levels.

cards.vorderseite: Lumbar spinal stenosis: features and treatment
cards.rueckseite: L4–L5 > L3–L4 > L2–L3 > L5–S1. **Neurogenic claudication**; lateral recess syndrome. Conservative ~3 months. Decompression ± foraminotomy; **fusion if instability/spondylolisthesis**. Relieves leg pain and halts progression better than back pain; ~70% good at 5 y.

cards.vorderseite: Rheumatoid arthritis of the cervical spine: indications for surgery
cards.rueckseite: > 85% radiographic involvement (atlantoaxial subluxation, pannus, basilar invagination, subaxial subluxation). **C1–C2 fusion** if symptomatic or asymptomatic with **atlantodental interval ≥ 8 mm** (6–9). Extend to occiput with basilar invagination. **Transoral odontoidectomy** for irreducible pannus/basilar invagination.

zeilen: Objective weakness, long tract signs, ambulatory
Objective weakness, long tract signs, nonambulatory

cards.vorderseite: Ankylosing spondylitis: neurosurgical relevance
cards.rueckseite: Young men, **90% HLA-B27**, sacroiliitis, uveitis. Rigid spine → **fractures after minor trauma** (75% cervical), pseudarthrosis; can develop OPLL/stenosis. Image the whole spine after any trauma. Surgery for fractures and fixed flexion deformity (osteotomy).

cards.vorderseite: OPLL: epidemiology and surgical approach
cards.rueckseite: Men, **East Asians** (> 10% of Japanese men > 60 y), onset ~50 y, 75% cervical. Can worsen acutely after minor trauma. Surgery for myelopathy: **anterior** decompression/fusion if < 3 segments localized, **posterior** (laminectomy, **laminoplasty**) for continuous multilevel disease. Poor recovery if > 65 y or myelopathy > 2 y.

cards.vorderseite: DISH: key facts
cards.rueckseite: Older white men (60–70 y). Thoracic 97%, lumbar 90%, cervical 78%. Flowing anterior osteophytes create long lever arms → **high fracture risk**. Surgery rarely, e.g. for **dysphagia** from anterior osteophytes.

cards.vorderseite: Syringomyelia: associations and treatment
cards.rueckseite: Chiari, myelomeningocele, tumor, infection, trauma (arachnoiditis). Classic **central cord syndrome** (dissociated sensory loss). Treat the cause (craniocervical decompression for Chiari), otherwise syringo-subarachnoid/-peritoneal/-pleural shunt, lysis of adhesions. Overall ⅓ improve, ⅓ stable, ⅓ worse.

cards.vorderseite: Myelomeningocele: epidemiology and management
cards.rueckseite: 1/1,000 births; recurrence 2–3% after one, 6–8% after two affected children (folate). Almost all have **Chiari II**; hydrocephalus ~75%. Keep moist, no pressure, antibiotics if ruptured; **closure within 36 h** (lowers infection, does not improve neurology); often VP shunt. Treated: 80% normal intelligence, 50% ambulate, 10% urinary continence.

cards.vorderseite: Tethered cord: signs and treatment
cards.rueckseite: Thick filum or lipoma, common after myelomeningocele. Leg weakness/pain, **bladder dysfunction**, cutaneous stigmata (hair tuft, dimple, nevus), **cavovarus feet**. Laminectomy and **detethering** ± lipoma resection; can re-tether with growth.

cards.vorderseite: Split cord malformation type I vs. type II
cards.rueckseite:
**Type I (diastematomyelia):** two hemicords in **separate dural tubes**, **osteocartilaginous** septum; cutaneous stigmata, mostly lumbar.
**Type II (diplomyelia):** one dural tube, **fibrous** septum.
Treatment: resect septum, reconstitute single dural tube, detether; watertight closure.

cards.vorderseite: Dermal sinus tract
cards.rueckseite: Mostly lumbar > occipital; **50% end in dermoid/epidermoid**. Skin dimple, hair, hemangioma. Risk of **meningitis** → resect down to the spinal canal and close the dura. Do not probe it.

zeilen: Complete: no motor/sensory function in S4–S5
Sensory incomplete: sensation (incl. sacral) preserved, no motor
Motor incomplete: > 50% key muscles below level < grade 3
Motor incomplete: ≥ 50% key muscles below level ≥ grade 3
Ipsilateral motor + proprioception loss, contralateral pain/temperature loss
Bilateral motor + pain/temperature loss, proprioception preserved; worst prognosis
Arms weaker than legs; hyperextension in a narrow (spondylotic) canal; best prognosis

cards.vorderseite: Acute spinal cord injury: medical management
cards.rueckseite:
- Immobilize (collar, board); clinical clearance only if alert, sober, no pain/tenderness, no distracting injury, normal exam incl. ROM (NEXUS), otherwise CT ± MRI
- Early **closed reduction** in awake patients with dislocation
- **MAP 85–90 mmHg for 7 days**
- **VTE prophylaxis**
- Methylprednisolone (30 mg/kg, then 5.4 mg/kg/h for 23 h) only as an **option within 8 h**; considerable morbidity
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 635. AANS/CNS 2013: steroids not recommended; AO Spine 2017: 24-h course an option if started < 8 h. Early decompression (< 24 h) recommended.

cards.vorderseite: Occipital condyle fractures (Anderson–Montesano)
cards.rueckseite:
- **Type I:** comminuted (axial load): stable → collar
- **Type II:** part of basilar skull fracture: stable → collar
- **Type III:** **alar ligament avulsion**: potentially unstable → halo/rigid collar 6–12 weeks (fusion if craniocervical instability)

cards.vorderseite: Jefferson fracture and the rule of Spence
cards.rueckseite:
Burst fracture of the **C1 ring** (anterior + posterior arch) from **axial load**; usually no deficit (fragments displace outward).
**Rule of Spence:** combined lateral mass overhang on open-mouth view **> 7 mm** → transverse ligament likely torn.
Intact ligament: immobilization ~12 weeks; torn: **C1–C2 fusion**.

zeilen: Worst healing: nonunion ~30% (10% if < 6 mm, up to 70% if ≥ 6 mm displacement). Surgery if age ≥ 50, displacement ≥ 6 mm, instability or nonunion
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 636. Surgical options: anterior odontoid screw (type II) or posterior C1–C2 fusion.

zeilen: Disrupted C2–C3 disk and PLL, displacement + anterolisthesis
No traction! Halo in extension 12 weeks
Plus bilateral C2–C3 facet dislocation, usually with deficit
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 636. Mechanism: hyperextension + axial load (diving).

cards.vorderseite: Atlantoaxial rotatory subluxation
cards.rueckseite: Children: spontaneous, after trauma or upper respiratory infection (**Grisel syndrome**), also RA. Torticollis ("cock robin"). **Traction reduction** (7–15 lbs children, 15–20 lbs adults); C1–C2 fusion if irreducible or recurrent.

zeilen: Morphology: none / compression / burst / distraction / rotation–translation
Neuro: intact / root / complete cord / incomplete cord
cards.notiz: CNBR Table 6.25. Total ≤ 3 nonoperative, 4 either, ≥ 5 operative.

cards.vorderseite: Unilateral vs. bilateral cervical facet dislocation
cards.rueckseite:
Flexion ± distraction.
**Unilateral:** usually **radiculopathy**, ~25% anterolisthesis; closed reduction; ligamentous or irreducible → open reduction/fusion.
**Bilateral:** usually **spinal cord injury**, **≥ 50% anterolisthesis**; urgent closed traction reduction in awake patients. MRI before reduction to look for traumatic disk herniation (especially if not examinable or before open reduction).

cards.vorderseite: Cervical teardrop fracture vs. clay shoveler's fracture
cards.rueckseite:
**Flexion teardrop:** anteroinferior body fragment + retrolisthesis of the body into the canal, disruption of disk, facets and all ligaments → **highly unstable**, anterior cord syndrome; anterior decompression + posterior fusion.
**Clay shoveler's:** avulsion of the spinous process (usually **C7**): stable if isolated.

cards.vorderseite: Denis three-column model
cards.rueckseite:
- **Anterior:** ALL, anterior anulus, anterior ½ of vertebral body
- **Middle:** posterior ½ of vertebral body, posterior anulus, **PLL**
- **Posterior:** pedicles, facets, lamina, ligamentum flavum, interspinous/supraspinous ligaments
Instability usually requires failure of **≥ 2 columns** (middle column is key).

cards.text: Thoracolumbar burst fracture, instability "50–20–50 rule": > {{c1::50%}} loss of vertebral body height, > {{c2::20°}} segmental kyphosis, < {{c3::50%}} remaining canal diameter.

cards.vorderseite: Chance fracture
cards.rueckseite: "**Seat-belt fracture**": flexion–distraction around an anterior fulcrum, horizontal fracture through all three columns posteriorly in tension. Usually **no deficit**, but **intra-abdominal injury in ≥ 50%**. Treatment: posterior instrumented fusion (purely bony injuries can heal in extension orthosis).

zeilen: Neuro: intact / root / complete cord–conus / incomplete cord–conus / cauda equina
Posterior ligamentous complex: intact / indeterminate / injured
cards.notiz: CNBR Table 6.26. Total ≤ 3 nonoperative, 4 either, ≥ 5 operative.
